title: Arts, special events and creative industries action plan feedback
subtitle: Council shared priorities on music, public art, communications, event sustainability and staff capacity, then authorized a closed session on land matters.
overview: Council held a special meeting to give feedback on the draft 2027–2030 Action Plan for Special Events, Arts and Creative Industries. No decisions on the plan were made. Staff asked for input on investment priorities, gaps in the draft and how to measure success, and said the plan will return to Council in late 2025 or early 2026.

Councillors backed expanded music development, better communication with residents, more opportunities for local artists and more public art, including Indigenous public art. They also asked for more consistent weekend programming, neighbourhood events and stronger cultural diversity. For events, Council ranked attendee experience and quality of life as the top measures of success.

Staff warned that demand is outgrowing calendar space and resources. Options include reallocating existing resources, adding operating budget and staff in future years, and choosing initiatives more selectively. Unbudgeted events also need flexibility. The one motion carried authorized a closed session after the meeting on two land matters {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a closed meeting immediately after the special meeting to consider a land acquisition matter and a land acquisition position and procedure for negotiation {{vote:m1}}.

debate: One councillor asked which action plan items would benefit the broader community most rather than individual artists. Staff replied that supporting artists first, especially in music, draws talent, venues and visitors downtown over time, and that culture also helps attract and keep workers.

Several councillors said communication is a weak point. They said many artists and communities outside the usual circles do not see city programs, and they asked staff to reach more diverse audiences. Staff said the Kitchener Live brand and a central place for public art calls should help.

One councillor said the capital items, such as the Homer Watson Gallery plan, should have been separated from the ranking exercise. Staff suggested ranking them low and noting the concern. Another councillor asked for film to be added to the list.

On special events, councillors supported the aim of being Canada's best host city. One said the goal should be realistic, such as leading in Southwest Ontario, while others said to aim high. Councillors also said events should stay affordable and that quality of life is a key measure.

Councillors raised sustainability. Suggestions included a sponsorship business plan, training for event organizers on finding sponsors, a restricted contingency for unplanned events, and volunteer incentives. Some worried about staff burnout and favoured fewer, better events, while others said more resources will be needed as the city grows.
